<button onclick="window.print()" style="float:right;margin-bottom:1rem">🖨 Print / Save as PDF</button>

::: {.callout-note}
## Overview
Barcoded Gel Beads, a cell suspension, and Partitioning Oil B are combined on a GEM-X 3' Chip to generate nanoliter Gel Beads-in-emulsion (GEMs) at limiting dilution, so most GEMs contain either zero or one cell. Reverse transcription inside the GEMs produces barcoded, full-length cDNA from poly-adenylated mRNA. After breaking the emulsion, cDNA is cleaned up, amplified, and a fixed 25% carried forward into 3' Gene Expression library construction (fragmentation, end repair/A-tailing, adaptor ligation, and sample index PCR), then sequenced.

Four steps: **1** GEM Generation & Barcoding → **2** Post GEM-RT Cleanup & cDNA Amplification → **3** 3' Gene Expression Library Construction → **4** Sequencing.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Before starting
- Equilibrate RT Reagent E, Reducing Agent B, cDNA Primers, Fragmentation Buffer, and Ligation Mix to room temperature before use.
- Prepare cell suspension in 1X Phosphate-Buffered Saline (PBS); **do not** add PBS directly to the suspension — PBS is added to the Master Mix instead (Step 1.2c).
- Prepare fresh 80% ethanol (15 mL per 8 reactions).
- Thaw Cleanup Buffer for 10 min at 65°C; verify no visible crystals before use.
- Vortex Dynabeads MyOne SILANE thoroughly (≥30 sec) immediately before adding to any mix — **do not** centrifuge beforehand.
- Firmware ≥2.0.0 required for Chromium X/iX; ≥2.2.0 for Chromium Xo.
:::

---

## Configure experiment

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof n_reactions   = Inputs.number({label: "Number of reactions (chip wells, ≤8/chip)", value: 1, min: 1, max: 8, step: 1})
viewof target_cells   = Inputs.number({label: "Targeted cell recovery (same target for every sample)", value: 5000, min: 500, max: 20000, step: 500})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof stock_concs_raw = Inputs.text({
  label: "Cell stock concentration per sample (cells/µL), comma-separated in chip-loading order",
  value: Array(n_reactions).fill(1000).join(", ")
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mm_scale    = (x, n) => x * n * 1.10   // standard master mixes: N reactions + 10% excess
plain_scale = (x, n) => x * n          // Elution Solution I: exact N×, no excess
fmt         = (x, d = 1) => x.toFixed(d)

stock_concs = stock_concs_raw.split(",").map(s => parseFloat(s.trim())).filter(n => Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0)

md`**${n_reactions} reaction(s) · targeting ${target_cells} cells/sample · ${stock_concs.length} stock concentration(s) entered**`
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Running more than 8 reactions
Only one GEM-X 3' Chip is used per run, with a maximum of 8 reaction wells. For more than 8 samples, run additional chips separately and repeat this protocol per chip (up to 8 reactions per chip's worth of master mix).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Re-entering concentrations after changing reaction count
Changing "Number of reactions" above resets the concentration field to placeholder values (1000 each) — re-enter your actual per-sample stock concentrations afterward, keeping the same left-to-right order you'll use when loading the chip.
:::

---

## Step 1: GEM Generation & Barcoding

::: {.callout-note}
## Objective
GEMs are generated by combining barcoded Gel Beads, a Master Mix containing cells, and Partitioning Oil B on the GEM-X 3' Chip. Cells are delivered at a limiting dilution so that the large majority of generated GEMs contain zero or one cell. Immediately after GEM generation, each Gel Bead dissolves and releases primers — Illumina TruSeq Read 1 + a 16 nt 10x Barcode + a 12 nt UMI + a 30 nt poly(dT) — which mix with the cell lysate and RT Master Mix. Incubating the GEMs then reverse-transcribes poly-adenylated mRNA into barcoded, full-length cDNA, with every transcript from a given GEM tagged with the same 10x Barcode.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Materials for this step

| Reducing Agent B | 2000087 | Vortex, verify no precipitate, centrifuge briefly | −20°C |
| Cell suspension | — | Place on ice | — |

| 1X PBS | — | Place on ice | — |

### Calculations for this step

**Master Mix** — used in Step 1.1. Prepare on ice, pipette mix 15x, centrifuge briefly. Add reagents in the listed order.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Inputs.table([
  {Component: "RT Reagent E (PN-2001106)",           "1X (µL)": 16.3, [`${n_reactions}X + 10% (µL)`]: fmt(mm_scale(16.3, n_reactions))},
  {Component: "Template Switch Oligo B (PN-2001027)", "1X (µL)": 3.1,  [`${n_reactions}X + 10% (µL)`]: fmt(mm_scale(3.1,  n_reactions))},
  {Component: "Reducing Agent B (PN-2000087)",         "1X (µL)": 2.0,  [`${n_reactions}X + 10% (µL)`]: fmt(mm_scale(2.0,  n_reactions))},
  {Component: "RT Enzyme E (PN-2001105/2001146)",      "1X (µL)": 7.0,  [`${n_reactions}X + 10% (µL)`]: fmt(mm_scale(7.0,  n_reactions))},
  {Component: "Total",                                 "1X (µL)": 28.4, [`${n_reactions}X + 10% (µL)`]: fmt(mm_scale(28.4, n_reactions))}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

Add 28.4 µL Master Mix into each tube of a PCR 8-tube strip on ice (1X per reaction, regardless of how many reactions the batch above covers).

**Cell Suspension Volume Calculator** — used in Step 1.2c.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not add PBS directly to the cell suspension
Add PBS to the Master Mix instead — see Step 1.2c below.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Math audit — reproduced from the source calculator table
10x Genomics ships this step as a large printed lookup table (Cell Stock Concentration × Targeted Cell Recovery, CG000731 p.34–35) rather than a formula. Back-calculating from >10 entries spanning both halves of that table gives a consistent relationship:

$$V_{cell\ suspension} = \frac{1.45 \times N_{target}}{C_{stock}} \qquad V_{PBS} = 36.6\;\mu L - V_{cell\ suspension}$$

where 36.6 µL is the fixed PBS + cell-suspension allowance (Master Mix 28.4 µL + 36.6 µL = 65 µL total per tube), and 1.45 is the recovery/loading factor implied by the table (≈69% capture efficiency). This reproduces every checked entry in the source table to within its printed rounding (±0.1 µL). If a computed cell suspension volume exceeds 36.6 µL, that combination isn't achievable — the source table greys these cells out ("exceeds allowable PBS volume"); dilute your stock or lower the target instead.

Since stock concentration is entered **per sample** above, this section computes cell suspension and PBS volumes **per sample** too — each tube gets its own mix even though every tube targets the same cell recovery.

<!-- TODO: this constant is empirically derived from the printed table, not stated explicitly as a formula in the source document. Sanity-check against CG000731 p.34-35 for your specific concentration/target if it matters for a critical run. -->
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
sample_calcs = stock_concs.map((c, i) => {
  const cell_susp_vol = 1.45 * target_cells / c;
  return {
    sample: i + 1,
    stock_conc: c,
    cell_susp_vol,
    pbs_vol: 36.6 - cell_susp_vol,
    achievable: cell_susp_vol <= 36.6
  };
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
stock_concs.length !== n_reactions
  ? md`::: {.callout-warning}
**${stock_concs.length} concentration(s) entered but ${n_reactions} reaction(s) configured above.** Enter exactly one stock concentration per reaction, comma-separated, in the same order you'll load the chip wells.
:::`
  : Inputs.table(
      sample_calcs.map(s => ({
        Sample: s.sample,
        "Stock conc. (cells/µL)": s.stock_conc,
        "Cell suspension (µL)": s.achievable ? fmt(s.cell_susp_vol) : "—",
        "1X PBS (µL)": s.achievable ? fmt(s.pbs_vol) : "—",
        "Total (µL, added to Master Mix)": s.achievable ? fmt(s.cell_susp_vol + s.pbs_vol) : "—"
      })),
      {layout: "auto"}
    )
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
unachievable = sample_calcs.filter(s => !s.achievable)

unachievable.length > 0
  ? md`::: {.callout-warning}
**Not achievable at the current concentration:** ${unachievable.map(s => `Sample ${s.sample} (${s.stock_conc} cells/µL) needs ≥${fmt(1.45 * target_cells / 36.6, 0)} cells/µL — dilute that sample's stock, or lower the targeted cell recovery for the whole run`).join("; ")}.
:::`
  : ""
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Low transfer volume
Cell suspension volumes below ~2 µL are hard to pipette accurately and increase cell-load variability — dilute the stock further for any sample where the table above returns a very small volume.
:::

---

### 1.1 Prepare Master Mix
*Assembles the RT enzyme, Template Switch Oligo, and Reducing Agent that will reverse-transcribe poly-adenylated mRNA into barcoded cDNA once combined with cells inside each GEM. Use the Master Mix table under "Calculations for this step" above.*

a. Prepare on ice, pipette mix 15x, centrifuge briefly. Add reagents in the listed order.
b. Add 28.4 µL Master Mix into each tube of a PCR 8-tube strip on ice (1X per reaction, regardless of how many reactions the batch covers).

### 1.2 Load GEM-X Chip
*Partitions cells + Master Mix, Gel Beads, and Partitioning Oil B into nanoliter-scale GEMs at limiting dilution, so most GEMs end up with zero or one cell. Uses the Cell Suspension Volume Calculator under "Calculations for this step" above.*

| Step | Action | Volume |
|------|--------|--------|
| a | If loading <8 reactions/chip, add 50% glycerol to each **unused** well | 60 µL (row 1), 60 µL (row 2), 250 µL (row 3) |
| b | Vortex Gel Bead strip 30 sec in 10x Vortex Adapter; centrifuge ~5 sec; check for bubbles | — |
| c | For each tube, add that sample's own PBS volume then its own cell suspension volume (per-sample table above) to its Master Mix; total 65 µL/tube for every sample | Per-sample calculator above |
| d | Load row labeled **1**: dispense Master Mix + Cell Suspension into bottom center of each well; wait 30 sec | 60 µL/well |
| e | Load row labeled **2**: aspirate Gel Beads (puncture foil first), dispense; wait 30 sec | 60 µL/well |
| f | Load row labeled **3**: dispense Partitioning Oil B from a reservoir, 2× 125 µL aliquots | 250 µL/well |
| g | Close chip holder (gasket attached); do not press on top of gasket; keep horizontal | — |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Partitioning Oil B is mandatory
Failure to add Partitioning Oil B to row 3 will prevent GEM generation and can damage the instrument. Run the chip on the Chromium X series instrument immediately after loading.
:::

### 1.3 Run the Chromium X Series Instrument
*Microfluidically drives cells, Gel Beads, and oil through the chip's channels to form the single-cell GEM emulsion.*

a. Eject tray; place assembled chip with gasket, keeping it horizontal; retract tray.
b. Confirm the GEM-X 3P program on screen; press play.
c. Run takes ~6 min; instrument chimes at completion — proceed immediately.

### 1.4 Transfer GEMs
*Recovers the GEM emulsion from the chip into a tube strip for thermal cycling. Abnormally high remaining volume in a recovery well is an early sign of a clog during GEM generation.*

a. Place a tube strip on ice.
b. Eject chip; discard gasket; fold lid back to expose wells at 45°.
c. Check rows 1–2 for abnormally high remaining volume (possible clog indicator).
d. Slowly aspirate **100 µL** GEMs from the lowest point of each recovery well (top NO FILL row) without sealing tips against the well bottom.
e. Dispense into the tube strip on ice over ~20 sec, tips against the sidewalls.
f. Start GEM incubation within 5 min. Route GEMs from separate chips to separate thermal cyclers if running back-to-back.

### 1.5 GEM-RT Incubation
*Performs reverse transcription inside each intact GEM, so every resulting cDNA molecule from a given partition carries the same 10x Barcode + UMI pair.*

Use a thermal cycler holding ≥100 µL (125 µL preferred, e.g. Bio-Rad C1000 Touch — use the highest available reaction volume setting on other instruments).

| Lid | Reaction volume | Run time |
|-----|-----------------|----------|
| 48°C | 125 µL | ~55 min |

| Step | Temperature | Time |
|------|-------------|------|
| 1 | 48°C | 00:45:00 |
| 2 | 85°C | 00:05:00 |
| 3 | 4°C | Hold |

Store at 4°C up to 72 h, or −20°C up to 1 week, or proceed directly.

---

## Step 2: Post GEM-RT Cleanup & cDNA Amplification

::: {.callout-note}
## Objective
After GEM-RT incubation, GEMs are broken and the pooled aqueous fraction is recovered. Silane magnetic beads (Dynabeads MyOne SILANE) then purify the first-strand barcoded cDNA away from the post GEM-RT reaction mixture, which still contains leftover RT enzyme, primers, and other biochemical reagents. The purified, barcoded, full-length cDNA is then amplified by PCR to generate enough mass for library construction.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Materials for this step

| Reagent | PN | Prep & handling | Storage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reducing Agent B | 2000087 | Thaw, vortex, verify no precipitate, centrifuge briefly | −20°C |
| cDNA Primers | 2000089 | Thaw, vortex, centrifuge briefly | −20°C |
| Dynabeads MyOne SILANE | 2000048 | Vortex thoroughly (≥30 sec) **immediately** before adding to the mix; if still clumpy, pipette mix to fully resuspend — do not centrifuge beforehand | 4°C |
| Amp Mix | 2000047 / 2000103 | Vortex, centrifuge briefly. **Do not** use Library Amp Mix (PN-2000531) here | −20°C |
| Cleanup Buffer | 2000088 | Thaw 10 min at 65°C, verify no visible crystals, cool to room temperature | −20°C |
| Recovery Agent | 220016 | — | Ambient |
| 10x Magnetic Separator B | 2001212 | — | Ambient |
| Qiagen Buffer EB | — | Manufacturer's recommendations | — |
| Bio-Rad 10% Tween 20 | — | Manufacturer's recommendations | — |
| 80% Ethanol | — | Prepare fresh, 15 mL per 8 reactions | Ambient |
| Beckman Coulter SPRIselect Reagent | — | Manufacturer's recommendations | — |
| Agilent Bioanalyzer High Sensitivity Kit | — | If used for QC & quantification | — |
| Agilent TapeStation ScreenTape & Reagents | — | If used for QC & quantification | — |

*Consolidated from CG000731 Rev B, "2.0 Get Started" (p.42).*
:::

### 2.1 Post GEM-RT Cleanup — Dynabeads
*Breaks the GEM emulsion and uses silane magnetic beads to purify barcoded, full-length cDNA away from leftover RT enzyme, primers, and other post-RT reaction components.*

a. Add **125 µL Recovery Agent** to each sample at room temperature. Do **not** pipette mix or vortex the biphasic mixture. Wait 2 min.
b. Slowly remove and discard **125 µL** Recovery Agent/Partitioning Oil (pink, bottom layer) — do not aspirate the aqueous phase.
c. Prepare the Dynabeads Cleanup Mix (above); vortex SILANE beads ≥30 sec immediately before use; do not centrifuge.
d. Vortex; add 200 µL to each tube; pipette mix 10x (pipette set to 200 µL).
e. Incubate 10 min RT, caps open; re-mix at ~5 min to resuspend settled beads.
f. Prepare Elution Solution I (above). Vortex and centrifuge briefly.

| Step | Action | Volume |
|------|--------|--------|
| g | Magnet•High until clear (white interface is normal) | — |
| h | Remove supernatant | — |
| i–j | Add 80% ethanol to pellet, wait 30 sec, remove | 300 µL |
| k–l | Repeat ethanol wash | 200 µL |
| m | Centrifuge briefly; magnet•Low | — |
| n | Remove remaining ethanol; air dry 1 min | — |
| o | Remove from magnet; add Elution Solution I immediately | 35.5 µL |
| p–q | Pipette mix 15x (set to 30 µL); incubate 1 min RT | — |
| r | Magnet•Low until clear | — |
| s | Transfer to a new tube strip | 35 µL |

### 2.2 cDNA Amplification
*Amplifies the purified, barcoded cDNA by PCR to generate sufficient mass for library construction.*

a. Prepare cDNA Amplification Reaction Mix (above) on ice; vortex, centrifuge briefly.
b. Add 65 µL Reaction Mix to the 35 µL sample from Step 2.1s. c. Pipette mix 15x (set to 90 µL); centrifuge briefly.

d. Thermal cycler protocol (lid 105°C, 100 µL reaction, ~25–50 min):

| Step | Temperature | Time |
|------|-------------|------|
| 1 | 98°C | 00:00:45 |
| 2 | 98°C | 00:00:20 |
| 3 | 63°C | 00:00:30 |
| 4 | 72°C | 00:01:00 |
| 5 | Go to step 2 — see cycle table below | — |
| 6 | 72°C | 00:01:00 |
| 7 | 4°C | Hold |

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
cdna_cycles = target_cells < 500 ? 13 : target_cells <= 6000 ? 12 : 11

md`**Recommended cDNA amplification cycles: ${cdna_cycles}**, based on the targeted cell recovery (${target_cells}) set above — a starting point that trades off final mass vs. amplification artifacts.`
```

e. Store at 4°C up to 72 h or −20°C up to 1 week, or proceed.

### 2.3 cDNA Cleanup — SPRIselect
*Removes unincorporated primers, enzyme, and small amplification artifacts via SPRI bead size selection, leaving purified amplified cDNA ready for QC and library construction.*

| Step | Action | Volume/ratio |
|------|--------|--------|
| a | Add SPRIselect (0.6X); pipette mix 15x (set to 150 µL) | 60 µL |
| b | Incubate 5 min RT | — |
| c–d | Magnet•High until clear; remove supernatant | — |
| e–f | Add 80% ethanol, wait 30 sec, remove (×2 washes total) | 200 µL |
| h | Centrifuge briefly; magnet•Low | — |
| i | Remove remaining ethanol; air dry **≤2 min** (over-drying hurts elution) | — |
| j | Remove from magnet; add Buffer EB; pipette mix 15x | 40.5 µL |
| k | Incubate 2 min RT | — |
| l | Magnet•High until clear | — |
| m | Transfer to new tube strip | 40 µL |

Store at 4°C up to 72 h or −20°C up to 4 weeks, or proceed.

### 2.4 Post cDNA Amplification QC & Quantification
*Determines total cDNA yield and mass, which sets the Sample Index PCR cycle count later in Step 3.5 — only a fixed 25% of this yield is carried forward into library construction regardless of the total (Step 3 Objective).*

Run 1 µL (undiluted for low-RNA-content cells <1 pg total RNA/cell; 1:5–1:10 diluted for high-RNA-content cells) on a Bioanalyzer High Sensitivity chip (or TapeStation/LabChip). Select the ~200–9,000 bp region and read the reported concentration (pg/µL).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Yield calculator (reproduces the source worked example)
$$Total\ Yield\ (ng) = \frac{Conc.\ (pg/\mu L) \times Elution\ Vol.\ (\mu L) \times Dilution\ Factor}{1000}$$
Only **25%** of total cDNA yield is carried forward into Gene Expression library construction (Step 3.1d).
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof qc_conc      = Inputs.number({label: "Reported concentration (pg/µL)", value: 2005.93, min: 0, step: 0.01})
viewof qc_elution_uL = Inputs.number({label: "Elution volume (µL)", value: 40, min: 0, step: 0.5})
viewof qc_dilution  = Inputs.number({label: "Dilution factor", value: 10, min: 1, step: 1})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
cdna_total_yield_ng = (qc_conc * qc_elution_uL * qc_dilution) / 1000
cdna_carry_forward_ng = cdna_total_yield_ng * 0.25

md`**Total cDNA yield: ${fmt(cdna_total_yield_ng, 2)} ng · Carry forward (25%) into GEX library construction: ${fmt(cdna_carry_forward_ng, 2)} ng** — see Step 3.5 for the matching Sample Index PCR cycle count.`
```

---

## Step 3: 3' Gene Expression Library Construction

::: {.callout-note}
## Objective
Enzymatic fragmentation and double-sided size selection optimize the cDNA amplicon size. P5 and P7 adaptors, i7 and i5 sample indexes, and a TruSeq Read 2 (read 2 primer sequence) are then added via End Repair, A-tailing, Adaptor Ligation, and PCR. The final libraries carry the P5 and P7 primers used for Illumina cluster generation and amplification.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Fixed-proportion input
Only **10 µL (25%)** of the 40 µL total cDNA from Step 2.3m goes into fragmentation — regardless of total yield. This is deliberate: library complexity (median genes/UMIs per cell) rises sharply with cDNA input and then plateaus well before 100% of the cDNA is used, so carrying forward more than 25% buys little extra complexity for the material spent. The remaining 30 µL (75%) can be stored at 4°C (≤72 h) or −20°C (≤4 weeks) for additional libraries.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

| DNA Ligase | 220110 / 220131 | Centrifuge briefly | −20°C |
| Library Amp Mix or Amp Mix | 2000531 or 2000047 / 2000103 | Vortex, centrifuge briefly | −20°C |

**Fragmentation Mix** — used in Step 3.1c.

```{ojs}

Inputs.table([
  {Component: "Buffer EB",                             "1X (µL)": 25, [`${n_reactions}X + 10% (µL)`]: fmt(mm_scale(25, n_reactions))},
  {Component: "Fragmentation Buffer (PN-2000091)",      "1X (µL)": 5,  [`${n_reactions}X + 10% (µL)`]: fmt(mm_scale(5,  n_reactions))},
  {Component: "Fragmentation Enzyme (PN-2000090/2000104)", "1X (µL)": 10, [`${n_reactions}X + 10% (µL)`]: fmt(mm_scale(10, n_reactions))},
  {Component: "Total",                                  "1X (µL)": 40, [`${n_reactions}X + 10% (µL)`]: fmt(mm_scale(40, n_reactions))}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

**Adaptor Ligation Mix** — used in Step 3.3a.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Inputs.table([
  {Component: "Ligation Mix (PN-2001109)",         "1X (µL)": 40, [`${n_reactions}X + 10% (µL)`]: fmt(mm_scale(40, n_reactions))},
  {Component: "DNA Ligase (PN-220110/220131)",      "1X (µL)": 10, [`${n_reactions}X + 10% (µL)`]: fmt(mm_scale(10, n_reactions))},
  {Component: "Total",                              "1X (µL)": 50, [`${n_reactions}X + 10% (µL)`]: fmt(mm_scale(50, n_reactions))}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

---

### 3.1 GEX Fragmentation, End Repair & A-tailing
*Enzymatically fragments cDNA to the target amplicon size, then blunts and A-tails the fragment ends to prepare them for adaptor ligation.*

a. Pre-cool thermal cycler block to 4°C before preparing the Fragmentation Mix.

| Lid | Reaction volume | Run time |
|-----|------------------|----------|
| 65°C | 50 µL | ~35 min |

| Step | Temperature | Time |
|------|-------------|------|
| Pre-cool | 4°C | Hold |
| Fragmentation | 32°C | 00:05:00 |
| End Repair & A-Tailing | 65°C | 00:30:00 |
| Hold | 4°C | Hold |

c. Prepare Fragmentation Mix (above) on ice; pipette mix, centrifuge briefly.
d. Transfer **only 10 µL** purified cDNA (25%) from Step 2.3 to a fresh tube strip. e. Add 40 µL Fragmentation Mix. f. Pipette mix 15x (set to 30 µL) on ice; centrifuge briefly. g. Transfer to the pre-cooled (4°C) thermal cycler and press SKIP to start.

### 3.2 Post Fragmentation/End Repair/A-tailing Cleanup — SPRIselect (double-sided)
*Double-sided size selection removes both oversized and undersized fragments, narrowing the library to the optimal amplicon size range before adaptor ligation.*

| Step | Action | Volume/ratio |
|------|--------|--------|
| a | Add SPRIselect (0.6X); pipette mix 15x (set to 75 µL) | 30 µL |
| b–c | Incubate 5 min RT; magnet•High until clear — **keep supernatant** | — |
| d | Transfer supernatant to new tube strip | 75 µL |
| e | Add SPRIselect (0.8X) to the transferred supernatant; pipette mix 15x (set to 80 µL) | 10 µL |
| f–g | Incubate 5 min RT; magnet•High until clear | — |
| h | Remove supernatant — **do not discard beads** | 80 µL |
| i–j | On magnet, add 80% ethanol, wait 30 sec, remove (×2 washes total) | 125 µL |
| l | Centrifuge briefly; magnet•Low | — |
| m | Remove ethanol — do not over-dry | — |
| n | Add Buffer EB; pipette mix 15x (set to 45 µL) | 50.5 µL |
| o–p | Incubate 2 min RT; magnet•High until clear | — |
| q | Transfer to new tube strip | 50 µL |

### 3.3 GEX Adaptor Ligation
*Ligates sequencing adaptors onto the fragmented, end-repaired cDNA — the substrate that P5/P7 and the sample indexes are later added to by PCR.*

a. Prepare Adaptor Ligation Mix (above); pipette mix, centrifuge briefly.
b. Add 50 µL Adaptor Ligation Mix to the 50 µL sample; pipette mix 15x (set to 90 µL); centrifuge briefly.

c. Incubate (lid 30°C — may be turned off if unsupported; 100 µL reaction; 15 min):

| Step | Temperature | Time |
|------|-------------|------|
| 1 | 20°C | 00:15:00 |
| 2 | 4°C | Hold |

### 3.4 Post Ligation Cleanup — SPRIselect
*Removes unligated adaptors and adaptor dimers before Sample Index PCR, preventing them from competing in the amplification reaction.*

| Step | Action | Volume/ratio |
|------|--------|--------|
| a | Add SPRIselect (0.8X); pipette mix 15x (set to 150 µL) | 80 µL |
| b–d | Incubate 5 min RT; magnet•High; remove supernatant | — |
| e–f | 80% ethanol wash, wait 30 sec, remove (×2 washes total) | 200 µL |
| h | Centrifuge briefly; magnet•Low | — |
| i | Air dry **≤2 min** | — |
| j | Add Buffer EB; pipette mix 15x | 30.5 µL |
| k–l | Incubate 2 min RT; magnet•Low until clear | — |
| m | Transfer to new tube strip | 30 µL |

### 3.5 GEX Sample Index PCR
*Adds the i7/i5 sample indexes and P5/P7 Illumina priming sites by PCR, amplifying the adaptor-ligated library to sequencing-ready mass. Cycle count is tuned to the cDNA mass carried forward in Step 2.4, since less input needs more cycles to reach the same final mass.*

a. Choose sample index sets so no indices overlap in a multiplexed run; record the Dual Index Plate TT Set A well ID used.

b. Add **50 µL** Library Amp Mix (PN-2000531) or Amp Mix (PN-2000047/2000103) to the 30 µL sample. c. Add **20 µL** of an individual Dual Index TT Set A well; pipette mix 5x (set to 90 µL); centrifuge briefly.

d. Thermal cycler protocol (lid 105°C, 100 µL, ~30 min):

| Step | Temperature | Time |
|------|-------------|------|
| 1 | 98°C | 00:00:45 |
| 2 | 98°C | 00:00:20 |
| 3 | 54°C | 00:00:30 |
| 4 | 72°C | 00:00:20 |
| 5 | Go to step 2 — see cycle table below | — |
| 6 | 72°C | 00:01:00 |
| 7 | 4°C | Hold |

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
si_cycles = cdna_carry_forward_ng <= 50   ? "14-16"
          : cdna_carry_forward_ng <= 250  ? "12-14"
          : cdna_carry_forward_ng <= 600  ? "10-12"
          : cdna_carry_forward_ng <= 1100 ? "8-10"
          : cdna_carry_forward_ng <= 1500 ? "6-8"
          : "5"

md`**Recommended Sample Index PCR cycles: ${si_cycles}**, based on the ${fmt(cdna_carry_forward_ng, 2)} ng carry-forward computed in Step 2.4 above.`
```

e. Store at 4°C up to 72 h, or proceed.

### 3.6 Post Sample Index PCR Size Selection — SPRIselect (double-sided)
*A final double-sided size selection removes residual primer/adaptor dimers and any oversized products, leaving a clean, sequencing-ready library.*

| Step | Action | Volume/ratio |
|------|--------|--------|
| a | Add SPRIselect (0.6X); pipette mix 15x (set to 150 µL) | 60 µL |
| b–c | Incubate 5 min RT; magnet•High until clear — **keep supernatant** | — |
| d | Transfer supernatant to new tube strip | 150 µL |
| e | Add SPRIselect (0.8X) to transferred supernatant; pipette mix 15x (set to 150 µL) | 20 µL |
| f–g | Incubate 5 min RT; magnet•High until clear | — |
| h | Remove supernatant — do not discard beads | 165 µL |
| i–j | On magnet, add 80% ethanol, wait 30 sec, remove (×2 washes total) | 200 µL |
| l | Centrifuge briefly; magnet•Low | — |
| m | Remove ethanol — do not over-dry | — |
| n | Add Buffer EB; pipette mix 15x (set to 35 µL) | 35.5 µL |
| o–p | Incubate 2 min RT; magnet•Low until clear | — |
| q | Transfer to new tube strip | 35 µL |

Store at 4°C up to 72 h or −20°C for long-term storage.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Peaks below 200 bp on QC?
Repeat this step: bring the library to 100 µL with nuclease-free water before repeating 3.6a. Expect ~40% material loss on a repeat. Alternatively, pool libraries destined to be sequenced together first, then run the pool through 3.6.
:::

### 3.7 Post Library Construction QC & Quantification
*Confirms the final library is free of sub-200 bp adaptor/primer contamination, measures average fragment size (used as the insert size for quantification), and determines loading concentration ahead of sequencing.*

Run 1 µL at 1:10 dilution on Bioanalyzer High Sensitivity (or TapeStation/LabChip); select the 200–2,000 bp region for average library size (used as insert size for quantification). Use a qPCR-based method (e.g. KAPA Library Quantification Kit) for the most accurate loading concentration ahead of sequencing.

---

## Step 4: Sequencing

::: {.callout-note}
## Objective
A Chromium Single Cell 3' Gene Expression Dual Index library is a standard Illumina paired-end construct beginning and ending with P5 and P7. The 16 bp 10x Barcode and 12 bp UMI are encoded in Read 1, while Read 2 sequences the cDNA fragment itself. i7 and i5 index sequences are read as separate sample index reads for demultiplexing. TruSeq Read 1 and TruSeq Read 2 are the standard Illumina sequencing primer sites used for paired-end sequencing.
:::

**Library depth & run parameters**

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Sequencing depth | Minimum 20,000 read pairs/cell |
| Sequencing type | Paired-end, dual indexing |
| Read 1 | 28 cycles |
| i7 Index | 10 cycles |
| i5 Index | 10 cycles |
| Read 2 | 90 cycles |

**Loading concentration by instrument**

| Instrument | Loading conc. (pM)* | PhiX (%) |
|------------|---------------------|----------|
| MiSeq | 12 | 1 |
| NextSeq 500/550 | 1.6 | 1 |
| NextSeq 1000/2000 | 650 | 1 |
| HiSeq 2500 (RR) | 12 | 1 |
| HiSeq 4000 | 240 | 1 |
| NovaSeq 6000 (Standard & Xp) | 150 | 1 |

\*Check the 10x Genomics Support site for current loading concentrations — these are periodically updated.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Index hopping mitigation
Store each library individually (4°C ≤72 h, or −20°C long-term) — **do not** pool during storage. Pool only immediately before sequencing; an extra 1.0X SPRI cleanup on the pooled libraries can remove residual free adaptors. Never pool two libraries sharing the same sample index in one lane — this breaks demultiplexing.
:::

Compatible sequencers: MiSeq, NextSeq 500/550/2000, HiSeq 2500 (Rapid Run), HiSeq 3000/4000, NovaSeq 6000. Data is analyzed with Cell Ranger (BCL/FASTQ → BAM, MEX, CSV, HDF5, web summary, .cloupe) and visualized in Loupe Browser.
